Subject: Follow-up: rate guard, burst behavior and unit-econ target for Greenline POC

Thanks again for the demo today — super helpful. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can finalize the POC budget:

- What Greenline needs: a 30-day pilot to validate recommendations generation (chat) + embeddings for search ranking.
- Estimated volume: baseline ~10M tokens/month (chat generation ~6M, embeddings net outbound ~4M).
- Peak behavior: marketing campaigns may produce bursts up to ~6M tokens/day for 2–3 days.
- Budget: target range $20k–$40k/month for the pilot. Crucially we need unit-econ targets: what would Redwood charge per 1M tokens at pilot scale, and what pricing for bursts / overages?

Specific asks: can you provide a simple table with (a) committed rate $/1M tokens at the pilot level, (b) burst allowance (how much free/soft burst we get and for how long), and (c) overage rate if we exceed quota? Also: what is typical lead time to increase quota mid-pilot if we need it?

Attached is our internal POC plan (greenline-poc-eval-plan.pdf) with expected concurrency and sample payload sizes. We want to align on economics before Legal routes an SOW.

Thanks — Evan

Evan — thanks for the clear notes and the attachment. High level answers below, plus a suggested Mutual Action Plan (MAP) to keep timelines tight.

Quick pricing sketch (pilot / hosted):
- Committed pilot rate (estimated volume 10M tokens / month): $95 per 1M tokens (volume discount applied to hosted list).
- Burst allowance: default soft-burst = up to 2x daily committed throughput for short windows (up to 72 hours) with automated alerts and throttles to avoid noisy failure modes. Soft-bursts are not billed at the committed rate beyond the reserved capacity; they incur an overage tier unless you opt for Dedicated.
- Overage rate (hosted, ad-hoc increases): 1.5x committed rate for tokens consumed beyond quota during the burst window (so ~$142.50 / 1M tokens at the pilot rate).

For customers planning repeated multi-day campaigns, we recommend either (A) a temporary quota increase (typically provisioned within 24–72 hours for hosted customers with review) or (B) a short Dedicated reservation for the campaign window (faster scaling and predictable unit-econ).

Other notes:
- Embeddings vs chat: embedding-generation tokens are billed the same token-based way; however, we usually recommend caching embeddings on your side to avoid duplicate calls.
- KV cache and prefix caching can materially reduce token consumption for chat follow-ups; we can run a quick pilot estimate once you share typical session lengths.

Proposed next steps (MAP):
1) Redwood sends a 1-page economics summary + pilot SOW (this thread) — by Wed 2026-06-09.
2) Greenline confirms pilot budget & signatory — by Fri 2026-06-11.
3) Pilot kickoff — target Mon 2026-06-21.

I've attached a draft SOW and a short pricing summary (redwood-pilot-sow-draft.docx). If that looks reasonable we'll route to Sales Ops + Legal for a 1-week turnaround.

If it's helpful, Ben can share a quick note on Dedicated vs Hosted math for your exact throughput numbers.

— Olga

Subject: Re: Follow-up: rate guard, burst behavior and unit-econ target for Greenline POC

Priya — good questions. A few concrete points from ops/pricing side: 

- Soft-limits & alerts: yes — hosted customers get soft-rate-limits (token throttling and informative 429s) + webhook/sms alarms at custom thresholds. We can set a 75%/90%/100% alert ladder.
- Overage billing cadence: billed monthly but calculated on actual token consumption; overage rate applies only to tokens above the committed quota for the billing period. For short burst windows we can apply a pro-rated approach for that billing period if you notify support within 48 hours and the burst is a rare occurrence.
- Emergency quota increases: staffed support can typically approve + apply a temporary quota uplift within 6–24 hours for most hosted customers; larger capacity changes (new Dedicated pools) take longer and are scheduled.
- Proposed numeric terms for pilot (to match your $20k–$40k target):
    * Pilot committed rate: $85 / 1M tokens (Redwood agrees to a 10M token floor for the pilot).
    * Overage (ad-hoc burst) rate: $127.50 / 1M tokens (1.5x) — can be capped with a committed cap after negotiation.
    * If you want stronger burst protection: short Dedicated reserve for campaign days reduces unit cost to ~$60 / 1M during the reserved window.

Next steps (quick):
1) Confirm which pricing lane you prefer (hosted pilot $85/1M with 1.5x overage OR short Dedicated reserve).
2) We share a 1-page SOW + DocuSign link for signature.
3) Redwood Ops sets alerts and a 75% pre-burst notification hook.

I'll add the pricing table to the shared doc and ping Sales Ops.

— Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
